accepted.evidence: Andersen's yam 'since' head compares RV yad and Pali yad and explicitly refers to the following relative ya- pronoun paradigm, which prints -am. Turner 10391 yá relative pronoun lists neuter Sanskrit yád, Pali yaṁ (sandhi yad-), and Ashokan neuter yaṁ/ye/e; this is the source's conjunctive use of the neuter relative form.

accepted.evidence: Andersen's am conjunction is glossed 'as, because, since', compares RV yad and Pali yam, records several inscriptions with am beside yam, and explicitly says 'cf. yam'. Link this source-marked reduced form to the same-function yam head and Turner 10391 relative family.

Andersen's independently listed Panguraria yate says 'for yam, see ya-'. The adjacent ya- relative pronoun paradigm and separate yam 'since' head trace to Turner 10391; preserve the printed exceptional form as a source variant of the installed yam record.

held.reason: The installed yata record merges two printed heads, 'where' (< yatra) and 'travel, going on, proceeding' (< yātrā). Their etymologies must remain separate until the homograph boundary is corrected.
